entries.title: A setting's name is a number
entries.means: Every setting in a container's environment has a name and a value. In {service}, one setting is named {key}. Docker Compose reads a name made only of digits as a number, not as a word. A name has to be a word, so Compose stops and will not read the file.
entries.fix: Put quotes around the name, so the line starts with "{key}": instead of {key}:. The value stays exactly the same. Fix it for me makes this change and shows you what it changed.

entries.sample: validating /tmp/x/compose.yaml: services.web additional properties 'restrat' not allowed
entries.title: A setting name Compose does not know
entries.means: Compose found a setting called {key} in {where}, and it is not one Compose knows. This is often a typing slip, such as a letter left out or the wrong capital. Compose stops rather than guess what you meant.
entries.fix: Look at the line with {key} on it. Check the spelling against Docker's page for this setting. If it is a setting you made up, remove the line. Then run the check again.

entries.sample: service "web" refers to undefined network backend: invalid compose project
entries.title: A network is used but never set up
entries.means: The service {service} is joined to a network called {network}. The file never says that this network exists. Compose will not start a container on a network it has not been told about.
entries.fix: Add {network} to the networks list at the bottom of the file. Or remove {network} from the networks of {service} if you do not need it.

entries.sample: service "web" refers to undefined volume data: invalid compose project
entries.title: A named volume is used but never set up
entries.means: The service {service} uses a volume called {volume}. The file never says that this volume exists. A named volume has to be listed in the file before a container can use it.
entries.fix: Add {volume} to the volumes list at the bottom of the file. Or, if you meant a folder on the server, start the path with a slash, like /mnt/user/appdata/name.

entries.sample: service "web" depends on undefined service "db": invalid compose project
entries.title: It waits for a container that is not in the file
entries.means: The service {service} is set to wait for a service called {target}. There is no service with that name in the file. Compose cannot wait for something that does not exist.
entries.fix: Check the spelling of {target} in the depends_on list of {service}. If the other container is missing, add it. If you do not need to wait for it, remove that line.

entries.match: yaml: line (?<line>\d+): mapping values are not allowed in this context
entries.sample: yaml: line 4: mapping values are not allowed in this context
entries.title: A line is indented wrongly
entries.means: Compose could not read line {line}. It has a colon where the file's layout does not allow one. This usually means the line is indented too far, or not far enough, so it does not sit under the right setting.
entries.fix: Look at line {line} and the line above it. Lines under a setting must be indented by the same amount, using spaces. Move line {line} so it lines up with its neighbours.

entries.match: yaml: line (?<line>\d+): found character that cannot start any token
entries.sample: yaml: line 3: found character that cannot start any token
entries.title: A tab character where spaces are needed
entries.means: Compose could not read line {line}. It most likely starts with a tab character. This kind of file only allows spaces for indenting, and a tab looks the same on screen but is not accepted.
entries.fix: Delete the blank space at the start of line {line} and type spaces in its place. Two spaces for each step in is the usual choice.

entries.title: A port is not a number
entries.means: One of the ports in the file is written as {port}. A port has to be a number, such as 8080, or a range of numbers. Compose cannot open a port it cannot read as a number.
entries.fix: Find {port} in the ports list and replace it with the port number. A port line looks like "8080:80", with the port on the server first and the port in the container second.

entries.match: service "(?<service>[^"]+)" has neither an image nor a build context specified
entries.sample: service "web" has neither an image nor a build context specified: invalid compose project
entries.title: The container has no image
entries.means: The service {service} does not say what to run. A container needs an image, which is the packaged app it starts from. Compose has nothing to start for {service} without one.
entries.fix: Add an image line under {service}, such as image: nginx:latest. Use the name of the app you want to run. If you build the app yourself, add a build line instead.

entries.sample: validating /tmp/staxx-explain/compose.yaml: services.web.ports must be a array
entries.title: A setting that needs a list
entries.means: In the {service} service, the setting {key} has to be a list of values, but the file gives it a single value instead. Compose cannot read one value where it expects a list.
entries.fix: Write {key} as a list. Put each value on its own line under {key}, starting with a dash and a space, such as - "8080:80" for a port. Then run the check again.
